switch_to_advanced_tip.ht: Show the full SCXtool interface with all tabs and options.

generate_apply_tip.ht: Generate the latest enhancements with your current settings and apply them to your game. A backup of the current global.ini is made first.

defaults_hint.ht:
Uses your current settings (the same ones the Advanced view shows).
The first run can take a few minutes while DataForge is extracted.

Switching to Advanced mode so you can set the game folder on the Config tab.

apply_enhancements_confirm_body.ht:
This will generate the latest enhancements with your current settings and apply them to your game's global.ini. A timestamped backup is made first.

The first run can take a few minutes while DataForge is extracted. Continue?

editor_tooltip.ht: Toggle the side-docked String Editor, a larger canvas for editing the selected row's custom value

tutorial_tooltip.ht: Start the guided tour of SCXtool's workflow. Runs automatically on first launch; click here anytime to replay.

restore_backup_tooltip.ht: Restore a previous global.ini from the backups folder. Up to 5 timestamped backups are kept; the oldest is pruned when a new one is created.

test_plan_tooltip.ht: Open the tester Test Plan: a checklist of what changed in this release, with progress tracking and a report you can submit.

switch_to_simple_tooltip.ht: Switch to the simplified one-button view.

reset_window_proportions_tooltip.ht: Restore the window size, panel layout and String Editor column widths to their defaults.

more_tooltip.ht: More actions: restore a backup, clear localization or cache, import or export, open the localization folder

osiris_github_tooltip.ht: Open the Osiris DevWorks GitHub organization

feedback_tooltip.ht: Open the SCXtool Discord channel for feedback, bug reports, and voting on upcoming features (requires joining the Osiris DevWorks Discord).

apply_enabled_tooltip.ht: Write the merged table contents to the game's global.ini. A timestamped backup of the current global.ini is created first.

apply_disabled_tooltip.ht: Already applied: nothing has changed since the last Apply to Game.

search_tooltip.ht: Show rows whose key, default, current or custom value contains this text (case-insensitive). Combines with the other filters.

ship_vehicle_names_only_tooltip.ht: Show only ship and vehicle name rows, hiding everything else including ship descriptions and all other categories. Leaves exactly the rows that favorites and ASOP sort order apply to.

category_tooltip.ht: Filter rows by domain (Ships, Ship Items, Missions, Gear, Commodities, Journal, Other). Categories are derived from the loc-key prefix.

status_tooltip.ht: Filter by status. Modified = you've set a Custom Value; Enhanced = produced by SCXtool's enhancements pipeline (ship stats, mission rewards, etc.); Unmodified = default text only; New = key exists only in enhancements/user.ini, not in the base file.

hide_unmodified_tooltip.ht: Show only rows where you've set a Custom Value. Same as the Status filter's Modified option but togglable on its own.

favorites_only_tooltip.ht: Show only rows you've starred as favorites. Favorites get a configurable prefix prepended to their name so they sort to the top of the in-game list.

bp_titles_only_tooltip.ht: Show only mission titles carrying the [BP] / [BP?] blueprint tag.

bp_descs_only_tooltip.ht: Show only mission descriptions containing a POTENTIAL BLUEPRINTS section.

group_sort_tooltip.ht: Sort titles and descriptions together for the same entity

clear_filters_tooltip.ht: Reset every filter (category, status, search, per-column boxes, checkboxes) so the full table is shown.

copy_filtered_tooltip.ht: Copy all visible filtered rows to clipboard (tab-separated)

preview_placeholder.ht: Select a row to preview its rendered text.

editor_underline_tooltip.ht: Underline the selected text (wraps it in <EM3>...</EM3>)

editor_highlight_tooltip.ht: Highlight the selected text with color emphasis (wraps it in <EM4>...</EM4>)

column_filter_tooltip.ht: Filter the {column} column. Filters across columns combine with AND.

editor_placeholder.ht: Select a row in the String Editor table to edit its custom value here.

order_tooltip.ht: Sort order: double-click to set a number for ASOP ordering

owned_tooltip_owned.ht: Owned blueprint — manage ownership on the Blueprint Tracker page

owned_tooltip_ownable.ht: Ownable blueprint — mark it owned on the Blueprint Tracker page

instructions.ht: Configure your Star Citizen installation path, extract base localization from Data.p4k, and import external INI files to customize your strings.

tools_desc.ht: Import an external INI file to merge custom strings into your user.ini. Keys are validated against base.ini, and conflicts are resolved interactively.

backup_desc.ht: Save all your settings — preferences, tag configurations, your Star Citizen folder, and your custom string overrides for every channel — into one small backup file. Import it on a new PC, after a fresh portable unzip, or to undo a misconfiguration. Backups work across SCXtool versions. Game caches are not included; they rebuild from your game files automatically.

export_settings_tooltip.ht: Save your preferences, Star Citizen folder, and custom string overrides to a small backup zip (a few KB). Keep it anywhere — cloud drive, USB stick — and import it later, on any SCXtool version, to restore your settings.

import_settings_tooltip.ht: Restore a settings backup zip made by any SCXtool version. Your current user.ini files are snapshotted first, your Star Citizen folder is restored (or auto-detected if the backup's path isn't on this PC), and SCXtool restarts with the imported settings.

installation_desc.ht: Path to your Star Citizen install root (the directory containing LIVE, PTU, EPTU, HOTFIX, TECH-PREVIEW).

map_language_desc.ht: Set a URL to each language's global.ini. When you switch to that language, SCXtool downloads it and uses it as the base strings, instead of the English Data.p4k extraction. The download is cached per language and only re-fetched when it changes. Leave a field blank to use the bundled default (if any).

base_localization_desc.ht: Extract global.ini from your installed Data.p4k to get stock game strings that always match your installed version.

data_desc.ht: Folder for user.ini, source cache, enhancement INIs, and backups. Move this off OneDrive-synced Documents if cache cleanup fails. The DataForge XML cache has its own path below — it’s ~1.4 GB so the default keeps it out of OneDrive automatically.

p4k_desc.ht: Extract global.ini from your installed Data.p4k to get stock game strings that always match your installed version.

p4k_status_found_no_base.ht: Data.p4k found  |  base.ini not yet extracted

migrate_data_body.ht:
Move your existing SCXtool data (overrides, backups, cached strings) from

{old_dir}

to the new folder

{new_dir}?

Files already in the new folder are kept. The old folder will be cleaned up after the move.

migrate_data_done_body.ht: Moved {count} file(s) to the new data folder.

channel_not_installed_body.ht: {channel} isn’t installed under the current root. Install it via the RSI Launcher or pick a different channel.

dataforge_cache_changed_body.ht:
Changing the DataForge cache path requires re-extracting from Data.p4k.

What should happen to the previous cache after re-extraction completes?

Apply Preview

include_new_tooltip.ht: When checked, items discovered from DataForge XML (status 'New') that have non-empty text will be included in the applied global.ini.

import_ini_tooltip.ht: Fold an external .ini into your overrides. A conflict-resolution dialog lets you decide per key: keep current, use imported, append, prepend, or provide a custom value.

reset_user_ini_tooltip.ht: Delete every custom string override for the active channel. A timestamped backup is saved next to the original so you can restore it.

restore_user_ini_tooltip.ht: Restore your custom string overrides from an automatic snapshot. SCXtool keeps the last few states of user.ini, so you can roll back a bad edit or recover after the file was emptied.

preview_apply_tooltip.ht: Dry-run summary of what Apply Enhancements would write — per-source key counts (with Enhancements broken down by category) and a Modified / Enhanced / Unmodified / New status tally. Nothing is written to the game until you click Apply Enhancements.

check_updates_tooltip.ht: Check GitHub for a newer SCXtool release.

theme_tooltip.ht: Switch the app theme. Takes effect immediately across the main window, toolbar, tabs, and Help panel.

disable_tutorial_tooltip.ht: When checked, the guided tour will not auto-launch on a new version. The Tutorial button in the toolbar still works.

game_path_tooltip.ht: Star Citizen install root — the directory that contains LIVE/, PTU/, EPTU/, HOTFIX/, and/or TECH-PREVIEW/. Auto-detected at install time; edit if your game lives elsewhere. The 'Channel' dropdown below picks which one the app reads and writes.

browse_game_tooltip.ht: Pick the Star Citizen install root in a folder browser.

channel_tooltip.ht: Star Citizen channel to read Data.p4k from and write global.ini to. Channels with no Data.p4k under the install root are disabled. Switching channels immediately reloads strings against the new channel's data.

language_tooltip.ht: Language to apply to the game. Keys missing from the translation fall back to English automatically.

map_language_tooltip.ht: Set a URL to each language's global.ini. When you switch to that language, SCXtool downloads it and uses it as the base strings instead of the English Data.p4k extraction.

data_dir_tooltip.ht: SCXtool's app data root. Each channel gets its own subfolder inside this directory. Leave blank or click Reset to use Documents\SCXtool.

browse_data_tooltip.ht: Pick the SCXtool data folder in a folder browser.

reset_data_tooltip.ht: Clear the custom data folder and use Documents\SCXtool.

cache_dir_tooltip.ht: Base folder for the extracted DataForge XML tree (~1.4 GB). Each channel nests under this as {base}\{channel}\cache\dataforge\. Defaults to %LOCALAPPDATA%\SCXtool so it stays out of OneDrive. Changing the path triggers a re-extraction.

browse_cache_tooltip.ht: Pick the DataForge cache base folder in a folder browser.

reset_cache_tooltip.ht: Clear the custom cache folder and use the platform default.

extract_tooltip.ht: Unpack stock localization (base.ini) plus the DataForge entity XMLs from your installed Data.p4k. Run after every Star Citizen patch — the strings reload into the table automatically when extraction finishes.

invalid_data_folder_body.ht:
The selected data folder is a file, not a directory:

onedrive_folder_body.ht:
This folder is inside OneDrive:

{path}

channel_not_installed_hint.ht: ⚠ {channel} isn't installed under this root — pick another channel

desc.ht: Optional features that extend the base localization data: category toggles for the enhancement generator, a favorites prefix for the in-game ship list, and a Tag Builder that customizes the bracketed name tags on components, missiles, and ship weapons.

enhancements_desc.ht: Select which enhancement categories to include. Click Apply to save changes. Enhancements are generated from your installed Data.p4k.

cat_desc_ships.ht: Ship performance, loadout, and crew data

cat_desc_missions.ht: XP rewards and blueprint drops for missions

cat_desc_journal.ht: Mining Compendium with crafting data per mineral

cat_desc_medical_consumables.ht: Plain-language effect summaries for CureLife medical pens

favorites_desc.ht: A configurable prefix is prepended to starred ship names in the generated ship list so they sort to the top of the in-game ship selection.

tag_builder_desc.ht: Customizes the bracketed name tags on components, missiles, and ship weapons. Changes take effect after clicking Save Tag Changes and re-running Generate Enhancements.

blueprints_desc.ht: Mark the blueprints you already own. Owned items get an [Owned] tag wherever they appear in a mission's potential blueprint rewards, so you can tell at a glance what's worth chasing. Select items on the left and use the arrows to move them to your owned list.

blueprints_empty_note.ht: Generate mission enhancements first to populate this list. Blueprints come from mission reward data.

blueprints_filter_note.ht: Type sorts everything into components, FPS weapons, armor, or Other. Class, Size and Grade apply to ship components only.

bp_scan_starting.ht: Scanning Star Citizen logs for received blueprints…

bp_scan_no_path.ht: No Star Citizen install path is configured, so there are no logs to scan. Set your game folder on the Config tab first.

bp_scan_none.ht: No new blueprints found since the last scan.

mission_field_ace_tooltip.ht: Show an "Ace Pilot: Yes" line in the mission details body when the mission spawns an ace pilot. The [ACE] title tag is a separate toggle under General Tags. Takes effect on the next Generate Enhancements.

mission_field_default_tooltip.ht: Show the {label} line in generated mission bodies. Takes effect on the next Generate Enhancements.

stats_prepend_tooltip.ht: Put the generated stats block above the manufacturer/PR description instead of below it (ships, components, weapons). Takes effect on the next Generate Enhancements.

standardize_ship_names_tooltip.ht: Rename exec-hangar (PYX) and Wikelo (WIK) ship variants to include a suffix that distinguishes them from the standard pledge-store version (e.g. "Anvil F8C Lightning PYX"). Takes effect on the next Generate Enhancements.

rs_ore_name_annotations_tooltip.ht: Append each mineable ore's base Resource Signature to its own display name (e.g. "Aluminium (RS 4285)"), so it shows up everywhere the game renders that name -- including the mission tracker. Independent of Resource Signatures under Mission Detail Fields. Takes effect on the next Generate Enhancements.

apply_categories_tooltip.ht: Save category selection. Unchecked categories will be disabled.

generate_enabled_tooltip.ht:
Generate enhanced localization files from your game's Data.p4k.
DataForge data will be extracted automatically if not already cached
(first run takes a few minutes; subsequent runs are fast).

generate_disabled_tooltip.ht: Already up to date — nothing that affects the generated output (categories, mission fields, stats/name options, Tag Builder) has changed since the last run.

favorite_prefix_tooltip.ht: Character prepended to favorited ship names so they sort to the top of the in-game ship list. Click Apply Prefix after changing to update all existing favorites.

rep_xp_label_tooltip.ht: Label for missions without a rank name (e.g. 'Rep: +100 XP')

header_em_tooltip.ht: Style for section headers: Underline (EM3) or Blue text (EM4)

prefix_enabled_tooltip.ht: Save the selected prefix and update all existing favorites to use it

prefix_disabled_tooltip.ht: Already applied — the selected prefix matches your current favorites.

annotate_mission_descs_tooltip.ht: When checked, the configured [CLASS-Sx-grade] tag is added to component names inside the POTENTIAL BLUEPRINTS list of mission descriptions. Uncheck for a cleaner mission body while keeping the tag on the actual component names elsewhere.

reset_tag_tooltip.ht: Restore the default pattern, mapping, and ordering for every category (Components / Missiles / Ship Weapons). Does not save or regenerate until you click Save Tag Changes or Generate Enhancements.

tag_enabled_tooltip.ht: Save the Components / Missiles / Ship Weapons tag configs and re-run the enhancement generator. New tags appear in-game after the next Apply Enhancements.

tag_disabled_tooltip.ht: Already saved — no Tag Builder changes since the last save.

tag_untick_exclude_tooltip.ht: Untick to exclude this element from the tag

tag_mapping_tooltip_ordinance.ht: Edit the Short / Medium / Long text used for each tracking type (e.g. Infrared → I / IR / Infrared).

tag_mapping_tooltip_damage.ht: Edit the Short / Medium / Long text used for each damage type (e.g. Energy → E / EN / Energy).

tag_mapping_tooltip_type.ht: Edit the Short / Medium / Long text used for each component type (e.g. Shield Generator → SH / SHLD / Shield).

tag_mapping_tooltip_label.ht: Edit the Short / Medium / Long text for the crafting label (e.g. Crafting → CF / Craft / Crafting).

tag_mapping_tooltip_collection.ht: Edit the Short / Medium / Long text for the collection label (e.g. Collection → Col / Collect / Collection).

tag_mapping_tooltip_default.ht: Edit the Short / Medium / Long text used for each class (e.g. Military → M / MIL / Military).

mission_detail_fields_note.ht: Unchecked fields are left out of mission descriptions. Applies on the next Generate Enhancements.

rs_ore_name_annotations_cb.ht: Show Resource Signatures (RS) next to ore names

forge_status_not_extracted.ht: DataForge: not yet extracted — click 'Generate Enhancements' to begin

forge_status_outdated.ht: DataForge: cache outdated — click 'Generate Enhancements' to re-extract and update

mt_enable_route_cb.ht: Add route to hauling mission titles

mt_standardize_cb.ht: Standardize hauling mission names (e.g. "Medium Cargo Haul" for every company, instead of "Large Shipment" / "Haul - Small Scale")

mt_route_hint.ht: The game fills in the real pickup and drop-off locations when the mission is accepted.

mt_shorten_titles_cb.ht: Shorten original titles (Shortens stock phrases, e.g. "Local Shipment Route" → "Route")

mt_shorten_sizes_cb.ht: Shorten cargo sizes (Abbreviates cargo sizes, e.g. "Extra Small" → "XS")

mt_general_tags_hint.ht: Show or hide these tags on the mission title only

mt_tag_rep_track_cb.ht: Rep Track Tag (adds "(Security)" / "(Contractor)" to the Rep tag)

mt_scanning_hint.ht: Recco Battaglia's Scanning/Mining missions target specific mineable ores, show each ore's Resource Signature value on the mission title.

scan_logs_tooltip.ht: Scan your Star Citizen log files (Game.log and logbackups) for "Received Blueprint" reward notifications and automatically mark them as owned.

scan_other_channels_tooltip.ht: LIVE and HOTFIX share the same account progression, so a blueprint earned on one shows up in the other's logs too. Also scans whichever of the two isn't your active channel, if it's installed. PTU, EPTU, and TECH-PREVIEW are separate test builds with their own progression and are never scanned.

force_rescan_tooltip.ht: Normally a scan only reads events since your last scan, so it stays fast. Check this if your Owned list looks wrong and you want to re-read every log from scratch instead. Unchecks itself after the next scan.

apply_owned_tag_tooltip.ht: Refresh the [Owned] tag on blueprint names in the strings table to match your current Owned list.

apply_owned_tag_tooltip_disabled.ht: Already up to date — your Owned list hasn't changed since the last apply.

owned_tags_refreshed.ht: [Owned] tags refreshed to match your current Owned list.

export_owned_tooltip.ht: Save your Owned list to a JSON or CSV file, for sharing progress with other tools or another SCXtool install.

import_owned_tooltip.ht: Add owned blueprints from a JSON or CSV file (including an scmdb.net export) to your current Owned list. Never removes anything already marked owned.

export_nothing_body.ht: Your Owned list is empty, so there's nothing to export.

import_nothing_matched_body.ht: None of the {count} blueprints in that file are currently tracked by SCXtool, so nothing was imported.

owned_added_singular.ht: 1 blueprint added to your Owned list. It'll show an [Owned] tag wherever it appears in a mission's blueprint rewards.

owned_added_plural.ht: {count} blueprints added to your Owned list. They'll show an [Owned] tag wherever they appear in a mission's blueprint rewards.

import_skipped_note.ht: {skipped} others in the file aren't currently tracked by SCXtool and were skipped.

min_level_tooltip.ht: Minimum severity to display. Entries below the selected level are hidden (DEBUG < INFO < WARNING < ERROR).

auto_scroll_tooltip.ht: Automatically scroll to the newest log entry as it arrives. Turn off to pin the view while inspecting older lines.

clear_tooltip.ht: Clear the on-screen log buffer. The session log file on disk is unaffected.

export_tooltip.ht: Save the current log buffer to a .log file — useful when filing a bug report.

keep_all_tooltip.ht: Resolve every conflict by keeping your existing value and discarding the imported one.

import_all_tooltip.ht: Resolve every conflict by accepting the imported value and overwriting your existing one.

dataforge_timeout.ht:
Converting the game database took longer than 30 minutes and was stopped.

The database found was {dcb} ({size} MB) at:
{path}

A healthy install converts in well under a minute, so this usually means SCXtool is reading the wrong Star Citizen folder. An old or leftover install still on your drive will look valid but hold outdated game files.

Open the RSI Launcher and check the install location it shows for Star Citizen. If it is not the path above, correct it in SCXtool's Config tab. If it IS the same path, run Verify Files in the launcher to repair the install instead.

cannot_save_edits_body.ht:

  {path}

{error_type}: {error}

The game file was NOT modified. Common causes:
  • Antivirus / Windows Controlled Folder Access blocking writes under the game folder
  • The user.ini file is open in another program
  • The drive is read-only or out of space

Resolve the underlying issue and Apply again.

Importing layers these over your current settings and replaces user.ini for the listed channels (your current user.ini files are snapshotted first, so this is reversible via Restore user.ini). Continue?

import_done_body_restored.ht:
Imported {applied} settings and string overrides for: {channels}.

Your Star Citizen folder was restored from the backup:
{root}

SCXtool needs to restart to load your imported settings. After the restart it will offer to regenerate and apply your enhancements.

import_done_body_detected.ht:
Imported {applied} settings and string overrides for: {channels}.

The backup's Star Citizen folder isn't on this PC, so it was auto-detected instead:
{root}

SCXtool needs to restart to load your imported settings. After the restart it will offer to regenerate and apply your enhancements.

import_done_body_no_install.ht:
Imported {applied} settings and string overrides for: {channels}.

No Star Citizen install was found on this PC — set it on the Config tab after the restart.

SCXtool needs to restart to load your imported settings.

relaunch_failed_body.ht: SCXtool could not restart itself. Please start it again manually — your imported settings will load then.

post_import_no_install_body.ht: Your imported settings are loaded, but no Star Citizen install is configured yet. Set the installation folder on the Config tab, then use Apply Enhancements to put your customizations into the game.

post_import_apply_title.ht: Almost Done — Apply to Your Game?

post_import_apply_body.ht:
Your settings are imported. The last step is to build your enhancements from this PC's game files and write them into the game.

Backups store your settings, not the generated game text, so this has to be done once on each new PC. It usually takes a few minutes — a little longer the first time, while your game files are unpacked.

You can also do this later with the Apply Enhancements button.

no_install_found.ht: No Star Citizen install was found on this PC's usual locations. Choose the folder that holds your LIVE or PTU folder on the Config page.

not_an_install.ht: {path} doesn't look like a Star Citizen install: it has no LIVE, PTU, EPTU, HOTFIX or TECH-PREVIEW folder.

generate_missing_body.ht: {count} enabled enhancement file(s) are missing for this channel and language. Generate them now from Data.p4k?

no_backups.ht: No backups yet: one is made each time you apply to the game.

detect_tooltip.ht: Search this PC's drives for the Star Citizen install the RSI Launcher is maintaining.

p4k_status_fresh.ht: Data.p4k found  |  base.ini is up to date

p4k_status_stale.ht: Data.p4k found  |  base.ini is older than the game: extract again

data_desc.ht: Folder for user.ini, the string cache, enhancement INIs and backups. Keep it off OneDrive-synced Documents. The DataForge cache (about 1.4 GB) lives in its own folder.

dataforge_moved_body.ht: The DataForge cache folder changed. Extract DataForge into the new folder now? Until then, generating enhancements will extract it first.

favorite_prefix_tooltip.ht: Characters put in front of a favorited ship's name, so favorites sort first in-game. Changing it re-prefixes every favorite.

import_summary.ht: {added} new key(s) will be added and {excluded} key(s) not in base.ini are skipped. {conflicts} key(s) already have a different value in your user.ini: choose what to keep for each.

category_generated.ht: Generated for this channel and language

category_missing.ht: Not generated yet: click Generate Enhancements

explorer_load_forge_tip.ht: Read the game database (Game2.dcb) and list every record as XML in a virtual folder beside it.

explorer_export_gamedata_tip.ht: Write game_data.json (ships, items, commodities and more) from the archive's game database.

explorer_empty.ht: Open a Data.p4k to browse its files. The selected channel's archive opens automatically when it is installed.

explorer_no_dcb.ht: This archive has no DataForge database (Data/Game2.dcb).

explorer_forge_failed.ht: Could not read the DataForge database

explorer_search_placeholder.ht: Search paths (text, or a pattern like *.dcb or Data/*/global.ini)

explorer_record_empty.ht: This record has no content; unforge writes no file for it.

explorer_preview_none.ht: Select a file to preview it

explorer_depth_tip.ht: How deep records follow pointers and references to other records. unforge's defaults are 100 and 1.

explorer_extract_count.ht: {count} selected items (folders include everything beneath them).

explorer_convert_cryxml_tip.ht: Binary CryXML files are written as text XML, as unp4k's unforge does.

explorer_extract_nothing.ht: Nothing to extract: the selection holds no files.

explorer_extract_failures.ht: {count} could not be extracted; see the details.

explorer_gamedata_desc.ht: Writes game_data.json from the archive's DataForge database: ships, vehicles, items, commodities, missions and more. A localization file resolves display names; an earlier game_data.json can fill in vehicle physics the database lacks.

update_check_disabled.ht: This build has no update source configured. Check the project's releases page for new versions.

desc.ht: Every mission and contract in the game files, with what it says, who offers it, what it pays in aUEC, reputation and blueprints, and the places it can send you. The game picks the exact place, and works out some payouts, when it offers a mission.

search_placeholder.ht: Search titles, contractors, descriptions, places, blueprints and factions...

no_data.ht: The mission list is read from the extracted game data, which isn't here yet.

no_places.ht: Your game data was extracted before mission locations were added. Extract it again to see where missions can send you.

select_hint.ht: Select a mission to see its details.

payout_calculated_note.ht: The game works this payout out when it offers the contract, from its difficulty and route. The amount isn't in the game files.

variants_note.ht: The game picks one of {count} versions of this text.

locations_note.ht: Every place this mission's location search can match. The game picks one when it offers the mission, and may narrow the choice by where you are.

no_locations.ht: No locations in the game files.

slot_runtime.ht: No fixed place: the game picks one tagged {tags} when it offers the mission.

rep_failure.ht: Reputation if it fails or is abandoned

desc.ht: Every ship's stock loadout from your game data, what it adds up to, and what fits each slot.

no_data.ht: The game data hasn't been extracted yet. Extract it to see the ships.

no_vehicles.ht: This game data was extracted before ship loadouts were added. Extract it again to read the ships' hardpoints.

reset_tip.ht: Put back the ship's stock loadout

auto_power_tip.ht: Split the power the way the game does by default

power_note.ht: Each component's power range and output are the game's. How the totals combine (cooling, signatures) is this app's estimate.

versus_kill.ht: Its vital hull is gone in

simulation_note.ht: Estimates: sustained fire that always hits, with shield absorption and resistance and armor deflection and reduction applied, and no shield regeneration. Quantum travel time includes spool.

picker_search.ht: Filter by name, maker or class…

desc.ht: Every Star Citizen option for the selected channel: gameplay, graphics, audio, controls, keybinds, and comms, VR and head tracking. Changes are kept here until you save them; saving backs up the game's files first. Close the game before saving, because it rewrites these files when it exits.

extracting.ht: Reading the game's settings definitions from Data.p4k

no_install.ht: No Star Citizen install is set for this channel. Choose the install folder on the Config tab.

no_data.ht: The game's settings definitions have not been read from Data.p4k yet.

load_error.ht: Could not load the game settings: {message}

running_banner.ht: Star Citizen is running. You can make changes, but they can only be saved after the game is closed, because it overwrites its settings files when it exits.

running_body.ht: Star Citizen is running. It rewrites its settings files when it exits, which would undo these changes. Close the game, then save again.

save_tip.ht: Writes attributes.xml and actionmaps.xml for this channel, after backing up the current files.

reset_tab_tip.ht: Returns every setting on this tab to the game's default. Nothing is written until you save.

reset_device_tip.ht: Removes every custom keybind for the selected device, so the game's defaults apply. Nothing is written until you save.

reset_tab_confirm.ht: Return every setting on this tab to the game's default? You can still discard the change before saving.

reset_device_confirm.ht: Remove every custom keybind for this device? You can still discard the change before saving.

backups_desc.ht: A copy of attributes.xml or actionmaps.xml is taken before every save and restore. The last 5 of each are kept.

restored.ht: Game settings restored from the backup.

search_placeholder.ht: Search settings, keybinds and console variables

pending_tip.ht: Changed here, not saved to the game yet

restart_tip.ht: Takes effect after restarting the game.

save_failed_title.ht: Could not save the game settings

verify_failed.ht: {path} did not read back as written.

discarded_body.ht: The channel, install or data folder changed, so the unsaved Game Settings changes for the previous one were discarded.

capture_keyboard.ht: Press a key or key combination. Hold Shift, Ctrl or Alt first to add a modifier.

capture_mouse.ht: Click a mouse button or scroll the wheel inside the box. Hold Shift, Ctrl or Alt to add a modifier.

capture_list.ht: Pick or type the input, for example button3, x, rotz or hat1_up.

input_devices_desc.ht: Inversion and response curves from the game's Controls menu, stored per device in actionmaps.xml. Dead zones apply to the selected joystick.

proximity_assist_landing.ht: Defaults - Flight - Proximity Assist for Landing On

ifcs_core.ht: Defaults - Flight - IFCS Core Functionality On

ads_padlock.ht: Look Ahead - Aiming Down Sights Enables Padlock

mode_tip.ht: Where details appear: in a pop-up when you hover over the (i) icon beside each item, or in a panel beside the list.

empty.ht: Hover over a setting to see its details here.

no_description.ht: The game gives no description for this.

option_desc.ht: Invert reverses this input's direction. The exponent shapes how it responds: above 1, small movements do less and the response builds toward the end of the travel; below 1, small movements do more.

axis_desc.ht: The dead zone is how far the axis has to move before the game responds. Saturation is how far along its travel the axis reaches full output.

has_curve.ht: Has a custom response curve, set in the game.

enable_cinematic_camera.ht: Lets the game briefly switch to cinematic camera angles at certain moments.

control_hints_enabled.ht: Shows the list of controls you can use right now in the corner of the screen. It changes with what you're doing.

vibration.ht: Lets a gamepad or other controller rumble.

camera_spring_movement.ht: Lets the camera lag slightly behind your movements and spring back, instead of staying rigidly fixed.

show_hints.ht: Shows pop-up hints that explain game features as you come across them.

ship_entry_labels_enabled.ht: Labels a ship's entrances, such as doors, ramps, ladders and elevators, when you're near it.

report_crime_if_ignoring.ht: When someone commits a crime against you, the game asks whether to report it. With this on, ignoring that notification reports the crime automatically.

text_input_repeat_delay.ht: How long you hold a key in a text box before it starts repeating, in seconds.

text_input_repeat_rate.ht: How many times per second a held key repeats in a text box.

star_map_zoom_speed.ht: How fast the star map zooms in and out.

contextual_dialog_subtitles.ht: Also shows subtitles for incidental dialogue around you, such as NPC chatter, not just conversations you're part of.

cockpit_audio_subtitles.ht: Shows subtitles for your ship computer's voice and other cockpit announcements.

sprint_toggle.ht: Press sprint once to start or stop sprinting, instead of holding the key.

crouch_toggle.ht: Press crouch once to crouch or stand up, instead of holding the key.

prone_toggle.ht: Press prone once to go prone or get up, instead of holding the key.

hold_toggle_zoom.ht: Press aim once to aim down sights and again to stop, instead of holding the button.

interaction_toggle.ht: Press the interaction key once to enter or leave interaction mode, instead of holding it.

input_prompt_display_input_icon.ht: Shows which key or button to press beside interaction prompts.

interaction_highlight_mode.ht: How objects you can interact with are highlighted when you look at them.

lean_toggle.ht: Press lean once to lean and again to straighten up, instead of holding the key.

crosshair_mode.ht: When the crosshair is shown while you're on foot.

crosshair_opacity.ht: How visible the on-foot crosshair is, from fully transparent to fully opaque.

hitmarker_mode.ht: Shows a marker on your crosshair when your shots hit.

weapon_mount_use_fpsrotation.ht: On mounted guns, the mouse aims directly, like an on-foot weapon. With this off, the mouse steers the gun like a turret.

ifcs_setting_auto_precision_mode_enabled.ht: Starts flights with automatic slowdown on, so the ship lowers its speed for you when you need finer control.

ifcs_setting_coupled_enabled.ht: Starts flights in decoupled mode, where the ship keeps drifting on its current course until you thrust against it. With this off, flights start in coupled mode, where the ship flies where you point it.

ifcs_setting_esp_enabled.ht: Starts flights with Enhanced Stick Precision (ESP) on, which slows your aim near a target to make small corrections easier.

ifcs_setting_gravity_compensation_enable.ht: Starts flights with gravity compensation on, so the thrusters hold the ship up against gravity without your input.

ifcs_setting_wind_compensation_enabled.ht: Starts flights with wind compensation on, so the ship corrects for wind pushing it off course in an atmosphere.

ifcs_setting_gsafe_enabled.ht: Starts flights with G-Safe on, which limits maneuvers so the pilot doesn't black out or red out from G-forces.

ifcs_setting_gsafe_disabled_by_boost.ht: Boosting turns G-Safe off while the boost lasts, so you can pull harder maneuvers at the risk of blacking out.

ifcs_setting_sticky_throttle_enabled.ht: Starts flights in cruise mode, where the throttle holds its position when you let go instead of returning to zero.

ifcs_setting_spacebrake_enables_boost.ht: Using the space brake also boosts, so the ship stops faster.

ifcs_setting_speed_limiter_on.ht: Starts flights with the speed limiter on, which caps your top speed at the limiter's setting.

ifcs_setting_proximity_assist_default_en.ht: Starts flights with proximity assist on, which slows the ship automatically to avoid flying into nearby objects.

ifcs_setting_proximity_assist_landing_en.ht: Turns proximity assist on while landing, to help you avoid hitting things on the way down.

ifcs_setting_stability_enabled.ht: Starts flights with stability assist on, which helps keep the ship steady.

ifcs_setting_command_behaviour_enabled.ht: Starts flights with the flight control system's (IFCS) command behaviour on.

ifcs_setting_core_functionality_enabled.ht: Starts flights with the flight control system's (IFCS) core functions on. With them off, your inputs drive the thrusters more directly, with much less assistance.

engineering_automatic_power_distribution.ht: When you give a component more power than its pool has free, the shortfall is taken from other power pools automatically.

light_group_controller_setting_lights_en.ht: Turns a ship's lights on automatically when you start flying it.

flight_thrust_invert_toggle.ht: On a HOTAS, the thrust-invert button switches between forward and reverse with each press, instead of reversing only while held.

flight_relative_throttle_trap_time.ht: With a relative throttle, how long the throttle holds at zero when you move the axis across its center, in seconds, so you don't slip straight into reverse.

flight_relative_throttle_trap_threshold.ht: With a relative throttle, how far past its center you have to move the axis before the throttle leaves zero.

flight_core_disabled_sensitivity_rotatio.ht: Scales rotation input while the flight control system's core functions are off. Higher turns the ship more for the same input.

flight_core_disabled_sensitivity_transla.ht: Scales strafing input while the flight control system's core functions are off. Higher thrusts harder for the same input.

flight_controller_setting_advanced_hud_s.ht: Shows the advanced HUD, with extra flight data, by default in SCM mode.

flight_controller_setting_advanced_hud_n.ht: Shows the advanced HUD, with extra flight data, by default in NAV mode.

flight_controller_setting_advanced_hud_l.ht: The advanced HUD shows text labels where it would otherwise use icons.

flight_controller_setting_course_predict.ht: Shows your ship's predicted course on the HUD.

flight_controller_setting_light_amplific.ht: Brightens dark scenes from the pilot's seat, like night vision.

turret_setting_light_amplification_enabl.ht: Brightens dark scenes from turret seats, like night vision.

velocity_indicator_display_type.ht: How the velocity indicator, which marks the direction your ship is actually moving, appears on the HUD.

weapon_setting_fallback_convergence_dist.ht: The distance, in metres, at which your guns' shots meet when no target is selected.

weapon_setting_gimbals_locked_pilot.ht: Starts with gimbals locked when piloting, so your guns fire straight ahead instead of following your aim.

weapon_setting_gimbals_locked_gunner.ht: Starts with gimbals locked when you're a gunner, so the guns fire straight ahead instead of following your aim.

weapon_setting_gimbals_locked_driver.ht: Starts with gimbals locked when driving a ground vehicle, so its guns fire straight ahead instead of following your aim.

weapon_setting_magnified_ui.ht: Starts with the magnified weapon display on.

weapon_setting_precision_lines.ht: Starts with precision lines on, which draw guide lines between your aim and the target's lead marker.

weapon_setting_staggered_firing.ht: Starts with staggered fire on, so guns in a group fire one after another instead of all at once.

weapon_setting_lag_pips.ht: Starts with lag PIPs on, which mark where your shots will pass relative to the target, instead of where to aim.

weapon_setting_single_pips.ht: Shows a separate PIP (aim marker) for each weapon instead of one combined marker.

weapon_setting_fading_pips.ht: Starts with fading PIPs on, which fade aim markers in and out depending on whether the target is in range.

manual_gimbal_mode_ships_default.ht: What manually aimed gimbal guns follow when you pilot a ship.

manual_gimbal_mode_ships_free_look.ht: What manually aimed gimbal guns follow while you use free look in a ship.

manual_gimbal_mode_mgv_default.ht: What manually aimed gimbal guns follow when you drive a ground vehicle.

manual_gimbal_mode_mgv_free_look.ht: What manually aimed gimbal guns follow while you use free look in a ground vehicle.

manual_gimbal_mode_turrets_default.ht: What manually aimed turret guns follow.

manual_gimbal_mode_turrets_free_look.ht: What manually aimed turret guns follow while you use free look.

missiles_increase_count_loop.ht: Raising the number of armed missiles past the maximum wraps back around to one.

bombs_desired_impact_point_direction.ht: How the desired impact point for bombs is placed.

vjoy_angle_pilots.ht: When flying with the mouse, how far the virtual joystick reaches, in degrees. The cursor at the edge gives full turn rate, so a smaller range turns the ship harder for less mouse movement.

vjoy_use_raw_input.ht: Feeds the pilot's virtual joystick unfiltered mouse movement.

vjoy_combined_dead_zone.ht: When flying with the mouse, how far from the center the cursor has to move before the ship starts turning, as a percentage of the virtual joystick's range.

vjoy_visibility.ht: When the virtual joystick is drawn on screen.

vjoy_show_deadzone.ht: Draws the dead zone in the middle of the virtual joystick.

vjoy_mgv_angle.ht: When driving with the mouse, how far the virtual joystick reaches, in degrees. A smaller range steers harder for less mouse movement.

vjoy_mgv_combined_dead_zone.ht: When driving with the mouse, how far from the center the cursor has to move before the vehicle responds, as a percentage of the virtual joystick's range.

vjoy_turret_angle.ht: When aiming a turret with the mouse, how far the virtual joystick reaches, in degrees. A smaller range turns the turret faster for less mouse movement.

vjoy_turret_combined_dead_zone.ht: When aiming a turret with the mouse, how far from the center the cursor has to move before the turret responds, as a percentage of the virtual joystick's range.

pilot_esp_strength.ht: How strongly Enhanced Stick Precision (ESP) slows your aim near a target. 1 is the game's default.

pilot_esp_dampening_amount.ht: How much ESP dampens your rotation input near a target.

pilot_esp_dampening_include_roll.ht: ESP also dampens roll, not just pitch and yaw.

turrets_esp_default_on.ht: Turns Enhanced Stick Precision (ESP) on by default in turrets.

turrets_esp_strength.ht: How strongly ESP slows turret aim near a target. 1 is the game's default.

turrets_esp_dampening.ht: The shape of ESP's dampening curve in turrets.

turret_default_mouse_mode.ht: How the mouse moves turrets by default.

turret_relative_mouse_mode_adaptive_zoom.ht: Lowers turret mouse sensitivity as you zoom in, so aiming stays steady. Doesn't apply when you aim with the virtual joystick.

salvage_free_gimbal_locks_rotation.ht: In salvage mode with a free gimbal, the mouse moves only the salvage head and the ship stops rotating.

salvage_aim_nudge_sensitivity.ht: How far the salvage aim moves when you nudge it.

tractor_beam_rotation_mode.ht: When you rotate an object with a tractor beam, it turns around its own axes instead of around your point of view.

targeting_show_heading.ht: Shows an arrow for the direction your locked target is heading.

targeting_show_distance.ht: Shows the distance to your locked target.

targeting_show_trail.ht: Shows a trail behind your locked target.

show_selected_target_reticle.ht: Draws a reticle around your selected target.

target_selection_direction_source.ht: Which direction the game uses to pick the target you're looking at, such as your ship's nose or your view.

targeting_pinned_overflow_behaviour.ht: What happens when you pin a target while every pin slot is full. With overflow enabled, the new target replaces the oldest pin; with it disabled, nothing is pinned.

auto_zoom_on_selected_target.ht: Zooms your view in automatically on your locked target.

auto_zoom_on_selected_target_strength.ht: How far the automatic zoom on a locked target goes.

targeting_arrow_display_mode.ht: How the arrow pointing to an off-screen target is shown.

look_ahead_enabled_spaceship.ht: Look ahead turns the pilot's view automatically toward where the ship is going, such as into turns or toward a target.

look_ahead_strength_forward.ht: How strongly look ahead keeps your view toward the ship's nose.

look_ahead_strength_velocity_vector.ht: How strongly look ahead turns your view toward the direction the ship is actually moving.

look_ahead_strength_yaw_pitch.ht: How far your view looks into turns.

look_ahead_strength_roll.ht: How far your view tilts into rolls.

look_ahead_strength_jump_point_spline.ht: How strongly your view follows the tunnel while you travel through a jump point.

look_ahead_strength_vjoy.ht: How strongly your view follows the virtual joystick cursor when you fly with the mouse.

look_ahead_strength_horizon_look_at.ht: How strongly your view is drawn toward the horizon when you fly near a planet.

look_ahead_strength_horizon_alignment.ht: How strongly your head tilts to stay level with the horizon.

look_ahead_strength_target_soft.ht: How strongly your view is drawn toward your target.

look_ahead_auto_target_padlock_enabled.ht: Turns target padlock on automatically when you lock a target, so your view follows it. Applies when piloting, driving and in turrets.

look_ahead_strength_quantum_boost_target.ht: How strongly your view turns toward your quantum boost destination.

look_ahead_dampening_zone.ht: The area around the center of your view, in degrees, where look ahead moves your view more gently.

look_ahead_ads_enables_padlock.ht: Aiming down sights turns target padlock on, so your view follows your target.

look_ahead_enabled_turret.ht: Look ahead in turret seats: your view turns automatically toward where the turret is aiming and toward your target.

look_ahead_strength_turret_forward.ht: How strongly look ahead keeps your view toward where the turret is pointing.

look_ahead_strength_turret_target_soft.ht: How strongly your view follows your target in a turret.

look_ahead_strength_turret_vjoy.ht: How strongly your view follows the virtual joystick cursor in a turret.

look_ahead_strength_turret_pitch_yaw.ht: How far your view looks into the turret's turns.

look_ahead_enabled_mgv.ht: Look ahead for drivers: your view turns automatically toward where the ground vehicle is going and toward your target.

look_ahead_strength_mgv_forward.ht: How strongly look ahead keeps your view toward the vehicle's front.

look_ahead_strength_mgv_target_soft.ht: How strongly your view follows your target while driving.

look_ahead_strength_mgv_vjoy.ht: How strongly your view follows the virtual joystick cursor while driving.

look_ahead_strength_mgv_pitch_yaw.ht: How far your view looks into turns while driving.

look_ahead_strength_mgv_horizon_alignmen.ht: How strongly your head tilts to stay level with the horizon while driving.

gforce_head_bob_scale.ht: How much G-forces move your character's head and view. 1 is the game's default; 0 turns it off.

gforce_boost_zoom_scale.ht: How strong the zoom effect is when you boost. 1 is the game's default; 0 turns it off.

shake_scale.ht: How much the camera shakes overall. 1 is the game's default; 0 turns camera shake off.

vehicle_weapon_recoil_scale.ht: How much firing vehicle weapons shakes your view. 1 is the game's default; 0 turns it off.

vehicle_seat_exit_needs_hold.ht: Leaving a combat seat, such as a pilot or turret seat, needs the exit button held for a quarter of a second, so you don't leave by accident.

show_party_nameplate.ht: Shows your party members' names above them.

party_nameplate_distance.ht: How far away, in metres, party members' names are still shown.

show_contact_friendly_nameplate.ht: Always shows names above friendly contacts.

show_contact_neutral_hostile_nameplate.ht: Always shows names above neutral and hostile contacts.

show_contact_distance.ht: Shows the distance to contacts beside their names.

friend_requests.ht: Lets other players send you friend requests.

friend_requests_notifications.ht: Notifies you when you get a friend request.

restrict_party_invites_notifications.ht: Whose party invites notify you: anyone's, or only your friends'.

restrict_currency_transfer_notifications.ht: Whose money transfers notify you: anyone's, or only your friends'.

restrict_comms_calls_notifications.ht: Whose comms calls notify you: anyone's, or only your friends'.

show_emissions_text.ht: Shows your ship's signature values as numbers on the emissions display, not just as bars.

lock_vehicle_ping_to_scan_mode.ht: The ping control only works in scanning mode, so you can't ping by accident.

show_scan_wave_highlights_vehicle.ht: Highlights vehicles your ping's scan wave passes over.

show_scan_wave_highlights_fps.ht: Highlights people on foot that your ping's scan wave passes over.

width.ht: The width of the game's resolution, in pixels.

height.ht: The height of the game's resolution, in pixels.

window_mode.ht: Whether the game runs in a window, full screen, or a borderless window.

vsync.ht: Matches the frame rate to your monitor's refresh rate to stop screen tearing, at the cost of some input delay.

aspect_modifier.ht: Adjusts the shape of helmet visor and lens displays to suit your screen, such as on ultrawide monitors.

qrcode.ht: Shows a QR code with your session's details on screen, which helps CIG match bug reports to game sessions.

upscaling.ht: Renders the game at a lower resolution and upscales it to your screen, for a higher frame rate. The percentage is the render resolution. Native AA renders at full resolution and only applies anti-aliasing.

upscaling_technique.ht: Which upscaler to use: CIG's own temporal upscaler (TSR), or NVIDIA DLSS/DLAA on NVIDIA RTX graphics cards.

upscaling_model.ht: Which AI model DLSS uses. The Transformer model generally gives a sharper, steadier image but costs more performance.

hdr.ht: Outputs a high dynamic range image to an HDR-capable display.

hdrref_white.ht: How bright normal white, such as the UI, appears in HDR, in nits. Raise it if the game looks dim.

hdrmax_brightness.ht: The brightest your HDR display can show, in nits. Set it to your display's peak brightness.

sys_spec.ht: Sets all the quality settings below at once. Settings left on "From quality preset" follow it.

global_illumination.ht: Quality of global illumination, which models light bouncing between surfaces.

sys_spec_object_detail.ht: How detailed objects and models are, especially at a distance.

sys_spec_object_view_distance.ht: How far away objects are still drawn.

sys_spec_texture_quality.ht: The resolution of textures. Higher settings use more video memory.

sys_spec_texture_detail.ht: Quality of detail textures, the fine surface detail you see up close.

sys_spec_texture_ground.ht: Quality of ground textures on planets and moons.

sys_spec_texture_filtering.ht: How sharp textures stay when seen at an angle, such as the ground ahead of you.

sys_spec_shadow_screen_space.ht: Quality of screen-space shadows, small contact shadows that add depth to fine detail.

sys_spec_planet_terrain_virtual_textures.ht: Quality of the textures on planet and moon terrain.

sys_spec_planet_volumetric_clouds.ht: Quality of clouds in planet atmospheres.

sys_spec_gas_cloud.ht: Quality of gas clouds in space.

sys_spec_fog.ht: Quality of fog and atmospheric haze.

sys_spec_water_caustics.ht: Quality of caustics, the rippling patterns of light that water casts on surfaces.

sys_spec_water_sim.ht: Quality of the water surface simulation, such as waves and ripples.

sys_spec_particles.ht: Quality of particle effects such as smoke, sparks and explosions.

sys_spec_shading.ht: Quality of shaders, which control how surfaces react to light.

sys_spec_post_processing.ht: Quality of post effects such as bloom, depth of field and lens effects.

sys_spec_video_comms.ht: Quality of video comms, the video feeds of players and NPCs during calls.

gamma.ht: Adjusts the brightness of midtones. Higher lightens dark areas without brightening bright areas as much.

contrast.ht: The difference between light and dark areas.

fov.ht: Field of view, in degrees: how much of the scene you see. Higher shows more around you; lower looks more zoomed in.

fov_social.ht: Field of view, in degrees, in social situations such as conversations.

fov_combat.ht: Field of view, in degrees, in combat.

sharpening.ht: How much the image is sharpened. 0 turns sharpening off.

chromatic_aberration.ht: Adds colour fringing toward the edges of the image, like a camera lens.

film_grain.ht: Adds fine film-grain noise to the image.

ignore_window_focus.ht: Keeps the game's sound playing when its window isn't in focus.

audio_ship_computer_speech_volume.ht: Volume of your ship computer's voice.

audio_simulation_announcer_volume.ht: Volume of the announcer in Arena Commander and other simulations.

video_volume.ht: Volume of videos played in the game's menus and screens.

audio_dynamic_range_preset.ht: How much the volume differs between quiet and loud sounds. A narrower range keeps quiet sounds audible and loud ones in check, which suits headphones or playing late at night.

audio_panning_rule.ht: Optimizes the sound for speakers or for headphones.

audio_ship_computer_verbosity_preset.ht: How often your ship's computer speaks up, from off to every announcement.

audio_shake_strength.ht: How much loud sounds, such as explosions and engines, shake the camera.

mouse_sensitivity.ht: How far your view moves for a given mouse movement.

adsmouse_sensitivity.ht: Mouse sensitivity while aiming down sights, relative to normal sensitivity. 1 is the same as normal.

zoom_sensitivity_multiplier_toggle.ht: Lowers mouse sensitivity further on sights that zoom in more, so aiming feels the same at every zoom level.

zoom_sensitivity_multiplier.ht: How much zoom scaling lowers mouse sensitivity while aiming down sights.

invert_ymouse.ht: Moving the mouse forward looks down instead of up.

mouse_acceleration.ht: Makes fast mouse movements move your view further than slow ones. 0 turns acceleration off.

mouse_smoothing.ht: Smooths mouse movement, at the cost of some delay. 0 turns smoothing off.

sensitivity.ht: How fast your view moves with a gamepad's stick.

invert_ycontroller.ht: Pushing a gamepad's stick up looks down instead of up.

aim_assistance.ht: Helps your aim stay on targets when you play with a gamepad.

hmd_vr.ht: Turns virtual reality on for a connected headset. VR support is experimental.

hmd_theater_mode.ht: Shows the game on a large virtual screen in your headset, instead of putting you inside the game world.

hmd_theater_mode_scale.ht: How large the theater-mode screen is.

hmd_theater_mode_distance.ht: How far away the theater-mode screen is.

hmd_theater_mode_curvature.ht: How much the theater-mode screen curves around you.

hmd_automatic_switching.ht: Switches automatically between full VR and theater mode, such as for menus.

hmd_ipdscale.ht: Scales the distance between your eyes in VR, which changes how large the world looks. 1 matches real scale.

hmd_infinity_projection_distance.ht: How far away vehicle HUD elements appear to float in VR.

hmd_monitor_mirror_mode.ht: What your monitor shows while you play in VR.

hmd_monitor_mirror_mode_smoothing.ht: Smooths the mirrored view on your monitor, so head movement looks less shaky to anyone watching.

hmd_actor_control_mode.ht: How your headset's movement controls your character on foot in VR.

hmd_actor_control_mode_ads_direct_offset.ht: When you aim down sights in VR, your aim follows your head directly.

hmd_reset_on_fps_ads.ht: Recenters your VR view when you aim down sights on foot.

hmd_fps_ads_dominant_eye.ht: Which eye lines up with your sights when you aim down sights in VR.

hmd_visor_aspect_modifier.ht: Adjusts the shape of helmet visor and lens displays in VR.

hmd_visor_distance.ht: How far from your eyes visor and lens displays appear in VR.

hmd_visor_height.ht: How high visor and lens displays appear in VR.

hmd_visor_scale.ht: How large visor and lens displays appear in VR.

hmd_visor_enabled.ht: Shows helmet visor and lens displays in VR.

hmd_uiscale.ht: How large menus and other UI appear in VR.

hmd_uidistance.ht: How far away menus and other UI appear in VR.

hmd_uiheight.ht: How high menus and other UI appear in VR.

hmd_cursor_size.ht: How large the 3D cursor is in VR.

hmd_cursor_sensitivity.ht: How fast the 3D cursor moves in VR.

hmd_cursor_follows_head.ht: The 3D cursor follows where you turn your head in VR.

hmd_cursor_use_eye_tracking.ht: Moves the 3D cursor with eye tracking, on headsets that support it.

hmd_mobiglas_distance.ht: How far from you the mobiGlas appears in VR.

hmd_gameplay_zoom_strength.ht: How far your view zooms in VR when you use zoom in gameplay.

headtracking_toggle.ht: Turns head tracking on, so your view follows your real head movement.

headtracking_enable_seat_position_offset.ht: In cockpits, lets head tracking move your head side to side, up and down, and forward and back, not just turn it.

headtracking_third_person_camera_toggle.ht: Head tracking also moves the external (third-person) camera.

headtracking_third_person_disable_during.ht: Turns head tracking off for the external camera while your inventory is open.

headtracking_disable_during_seat.ht: Turns head tracking off while you're seated.

headtracking_disable_during_walking.ht: Turns head tracking off while you're on foot.

headtracking_disable_during_ads.ht: Turns head tracking off while you aim down sights.

headtracking_disable_during_mobi_glas.ht: Turns head tracking off while your mobiGlas is open.

headtracking_disable_during_im.ht: Turns head tracking off while you're in interaction mode.

headtracking_disable_during_vehicle_ads.ht: Turns head tracking off while you use precision targeting in a vehicle.

headtracking_toggle_auto_calibrate.ht: Recenters head tracking automatically when you turn it on.

headtracking_source.ht: Which head-tracking device or software to use.

headtracking_enable_roll_seat.ht: Lets your view tilt with your head while you're seated.

headtracking_enable_roll_fps.ht: Lets your view tilt with your head while you're on foot.

headtracking_hold_use_raw_during_hold.ht: While you hold the head-tracking button, your view follows the tracker's raw position instead of the recentered one.

headtracking_inactivity_time.ht: Turns head tracking off after this many seconds without input from the tracker.

headtracking_global_smoothing_position.ht: Smooths head-tracking position. 0 turns smoothing off.

headtracking_global_smoothing_rotation.ht: Smooths head-tracking rotation. 0 turns smoothing off.

preferred_audio_input_device_hash.ht: Which microphone the game uses for voice chat.

mute_microphone_vo_ip.ht: Mutes your microphone in voice chat.

microphone_volume.ht: How loud your microphone is to other players, in percent.

audio_voipvolume.ht: How loud other players' voices are.

enable_level_activated_voice_transmissio.ht: Transmits your voice automatically when you speak loudly enough, instead of only while you hold push-to-talk.

voice_level_on_threshold.ht: How loud you have to speak, in decibels, before voice activation starts transmitting. Values closer to 0 need a louder voice.

fo_ipcamera_selection.ht: Which webcam to use for facial tracking.

fo_ipcamera_rotation.ht: Rotates the webcam image for facial tracking, for cameras mounted sideways or upside down.

head_tracking_faceware_pitch_multiplier.ht: How far your view tilts up and down for a given head movement, when a webcam tracks your head.

head_tracking_faceware_yaw_multiplier.ht: How far your view turns left and right for a given head movement, when a webcam tracks your head.

head_tracking_faceware_roll_multiplier.ht: How far your view rolls for a given head tilt, when a webcam tracks your head.

head_tracking_face_ware_deadzone_offset.ht: How far, in degrees, your head has to move before webcam head tracking responds.

head_tracking_face_ware_deadzone_rotatio.ht: How far, in degrees, you can turn your head left or right from center before webcam tracking turns your view.
How far, in degrees, you can tilt your head up or down from center before webcam tracking tilts your view.
How far, in degrees, you can tilt your head sideways from center before webcam tracking rolls your view.

head_tracking_face_ware_smoothing.ht: How quickly webcam head tracking follows your movement. Lower values are smoother but slower.

head_tracking_face_ware_position_scale.ht: How far your view moves for a given head movement when a webcam tracks your head's position.

head_tracking_face_ware_position_dead_zo.ht: How far you can move your head left or right before webcam tracking moves your view.
How far you can move your head up or down before webcam tracking moves your view.
How far you can move your head forward or back before webcam tracking moves your view.

head_tracking_face_ware_couple_position_.ht: Shifts your view's position as you turn your head, the way a real head moves, when a webcam tracks your head.

tobii_enabled.ht: Turns on Tobii extended view, where your view follows your eyes and head.

tobii_head_position_scale.ht: How far your view moves for a given head movement with Tobii.

tobii_head_position_dead_zone_x.ht: How far you can move your head left or right before Tobii moves your view.

tobii_head_position_dead_zone_y.ht: How far you can move your head forward or back before Tobii moves your view.

tobii_head_position_dead_zone_z.ht: How far you can move your head up or down before Tobii moves your view.

tobii_couple_position_offset_to_orientat.ht: Shifts your view's position as you turn your head, the way a real head moves, with Tobii.

tobii_gaze_based_target_selection.ht: Selects targets by looking at them.

tobii_gaze_based_missile_lock.ht: Locks missiles onto what you're looking at.

tobii_gaze_based_bomb_desired_impact_poi.ht: Sets where your bombs should land by looking at the spot.

tobii_gaze_input_method_profile0.ht: How your gaze moves your view while you're seated.

tobii_camera_boost_value_profile0.ht: While seated, how much further your view turns when you look toward the edge of the screen.

tobii_camera_boost_gaze_deadzone_profile.ht: While seated, how far from the center of the screen you have to look before the camera boost starts.

tobii_input_mix_eye_head_tracking_ratio_.ht: While seated, how much your view follows your eyes versus your head, from 0 (eyes only) to 1 (head only).

tobii_input_mix_gaze_responsiveness_prof.ht: While seated, how quickly your view reacts to where you look.

tobii_head_sensitivity_yaw_profile0.ht: While seated, how far your view turns left and right for a given head movement.

tobii_head_sensitivity_pitch_profile0.ht: While seated, how far your view tilts up and down for a given head movement.

tobii_head_sensitivity_roll_profile0.ht: While seated, how far your view rolls for a given head tilt.

tobii_head_center_stabilization_profile0.ht: While seated, steadies your view while you look near the center of the screen.

tobii_head_view_auto_center_profile0.ht: While seated, recenters your view automatically when you look back at the center of the screen.

tobii_gaze_input_method_profile1.ht: How your gaze moves your view while you're on foot.

tobii_camera_boost_value_profile1.ht: On foot, how much further your view turns when you look toward the edge of the screen.

tobii_camera_boost_gaze_deadzone_profile.ht: On foot, how far from the center of the screen you have to look before the camera boost starts.

tobii_input_mix_eye_head_tracking_ratio_.ht: On foot, how much your view follows your eyes versus your head, from 0 (eyes only) to 1 (head only).

tobii_input_mix_gaze_responsiveness_prof.ht: On foot, how quickly your view reacts to where you look.

tobii_head_sensitivity_yaw_profile1.ht: On foot, how far your view turns left and right for a given head movement.

tobii_head_sensitivity_pitch_profile1.ht: On foot, how far your view tilts up and down for a given head movement.

tobii_head_sensitivity_roll_profile1.ht: On foot, how far your view rolls for a given head tilt.

tobii_head_center_stabilization_profile1.ht: On foot, steadies your view while you look near the center of the screen.

tobii_head_view_auto_center_profile1.ht: On foot, recenters your view automatically when you look back at the center of the screen.
